title: Microsoft Entra ID, authentication methods and external identities
learningObjective: Describe Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Domain Services, SSO, MFA and passwordless authentication, and external identities.
foundation: Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud identity service. It signs users in to Azure, Microsoft 365 and thousands of other apps, and protects those sign-ins.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services gives you an old-style Windows domain (domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, Kerberos) as a managed service, for legacy apps, without running domain controllers yourself.
Authentication proves who you are. SSO: sign in once, use many apps. MFA: a password plus something you have (phone) or are (fingerprint). Passwordless: no password at all.
External identities let people outside your organisation (partners, customers) sign in to your apps with their own accounts.
engineer: Entra ID capabilities: authentication (verify identity, self-service password reset, MFA, banned password lists, smart lockout), single sign-on, application management, device management (register devices, Intune policies). Hybrid: Microsoft Entra Connect synchronises on-premises AD identities to Entra ID.

Entra Domain Services: managed domain with two domain controllers deployed and maintained by Microsoft; one-way sync from Entra ID; supports legacy protocols (Kerberos, NTLM, LDAP) and Group Policy for lift-and-shift apps. It's not a replacement for on-premises AD and doesn't sync back.

MFA factors: something you know (password), something you have (phone, hardware key), something you are (fingerprint, face). Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication supports Authenticator app notifications, codes, SMS and voice.
Passwordless options: Windows Hello for Business (biometric/PIN tied to a device), Microsoft Authenticator app, FIDO2 security keys, and passkeys. Phishing-resistant and convenient.

External identities (Microsoft Entra External ID): B2B collaboration (invite partners as guest users who use their own identity), B2B direct connect (mutual trust, for Teams shared channels), and External ID for customers (sign-up/sign-in for consumer and business customer apps, including social providers). Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2 add Conditional Access and identity protection for guests too.

example.title: A consultancy
body: Staff sign in once to Microsoft 365, the Azure portal and Salesforce (SSO) using Windows Hello (passwordless). Contractors must approve an Authenticator notification (MFA).
Client employees are invited as B2B guests to a project site using their own company accounts, and an old timesheet app moved to Azure joins a Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: User Administrator or Global Administrator for identity settings
portal: Microsoft Entra admin center > Users / Groups / External Identities.
Protection > Authentication methods: enable passkeys, Authenticator, FIDO2.

troubleshooting.symptom: A legacy app requires LDAP binds in Azure.
Partners need accounts in your tenant and forget passwords.
troubleshooting.cause: Local accounts were created for them.
troubleshooting.fix: Use B2B collaboration so they use their own identity.

comparisons.service: Entra ID vs Active Directory Domain Services
comparisons.difference: Entra ID is cloud identity using modern protocols (OAuth, SAML, OpenID Connect); AD DS is on-premises using Kerberos/LDAP.

comparisons.service: B2B vs External ID for customers
comparisons.difference: B2B is for partners collaborating in your workforce tenant; customer identity is for consumer-facing apps.

misconceptions.myth: Entra ID is just Active Directory in the cloud.
misconceptions.reality: It's a different service with modern protocols.
With MFA and Conditional Access, SSO reduces password reuse.

misconceptions.myth: Guests need accounts created for them.
misconceptions.reality: They sign in with their own identity.

architectureDecisions: Turn on MFA for everyone; move to passwordless where possible.
Use B2B for partner access instead of local accounts.
Use Domain Services only for legacy needs.
